correctness.rationale: The event that y has no outgoing path of length at most two to x is exactly that x covers y. A fixed x covering y requires x→y and independently forbids (0,1) at every remaining label; conditioning therefore leaves iid uniform (1,1),(1,0),(0,0) marks and fair independent edges among the remaining labels. In the second Bonferroni sum, shared-coverer and shared-covered pairs have 5/8 allowed patterns per outside label; chains have 4/8; opposed directions are incompatible; disjoint endpoints have 9/16. Independently enumerated both the outside patterns and the internal orientations (2/8 for either same-role overlap, 1/8 for a chain, 0/2 for opposition, 6/64 for disjoint endpoints). Replay: python3 /workspace/frozen_review_arithmetic.py (requires SymPy; no frozen code executed). Summing O(n^3) or O(n^4) pairs and dividing by mu=E W=n(n-1)(3/4)^(n-2)/2 gives the stated bound, including the negligible chain term. Multiple covers have unconditional probability at most the Bonferroni sum. For the full marked tournament the total-variation identity is exact: on a tournament T with W>0 the chosen mark has mass P(T)/P(F), whereas sampling a uniformly chosen specified cover first gives mass P(T)/mu for each valid mark at T. Their total overlap is P(F)/mu, and projection to the pair and array can only decrease TV. Scores under the reference are (1+A+B,A), giving the stated iid bivariate CLT with covariance (2,1;1,2)/9 and O(1) centering shifts. Other vertices have Bin(n-3,1/2) scores on the outside subgraph plus at most two, so a union of Hoeffding bounds separates all of them from the two marked scores with probability 1-o(1); it does not require independent scores across outside vertices. TV transfers the separation and conditional uniqueness identifies the sole covered vertex. The claim is rank recovery given the rare event, not a test for its existence from the scores of an unconditional tournament. Read the frozen verification note and enumerator; its tests are finite and do not prove these limiting assertions.

value.rationale: The useful output is structural identification, not another small improvement in the probability of universal kingship. Given a failure, one can typically locate both labels of the exceptional covering relation from the strict global score extremes without checking all pairwise length-two paths. The theorem also distinguishes its strongly polarized bivariate conditional score law from the fair, near-half scores of the rest of the tournament. These claims have precise scope and do not assert that an unconditional tournament's extreme scores certify failure.
